input:
Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Offshore Energy Installation Safety Directive (OEISD) below. No regulator summary has been provided.

---
PRIOR TEXT — OEISD Edition 3, Articles 1–7
---

Article 1. Scope
This Directive applies to all offshore energy installations operating within the Exclusive Economic Zone of Veldrath, including fixed platforms, floating production units, and subsea infrastructure with a rated power output exceeding 5 MW.

Article 2. Safety Case Submission
Operators shall submit a Safety Case to the Veldrath Offshore Safety Authority (VOSA) at least 180 days before commencing production operations. The Safety Case shall describe all major hazard scenarios and the control measures in place.

Article 3. Competency Assurance
Operators shall maintain a competency assurance framework for all personnel engaged in safety-critical activities. The framework shall include regular assessment of individual competency against defined role requirements.

Article 4. Emergency Response Plan
Operators shall prepare and maintain an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) covering well control, fire, explosion, and hydrocarbon release scenarios. The ERP shall be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 24 months.

Article 5. Well Notification
Prior to the commencement of any well operation, operators shall notify VOSA in writing at least 21 days in advance, providing the well programme and the identity of the well operator.

Article 6. Incident Reporting
Operators shall report to VOSA any dangerous occurrence or occupational injury resulting in absence from work exceeding three consecutive days. Reports shall be submitted within 72 hours of the operator becoming aware of the incident.

Article 7. Records Retention
Operators shall retain all records required under this Directive for a minimum period of five years from the date of creation.

---
NEW TEXT — OEISD Edition 4, Articles 1–8
---

Article 1. Scope
This Directive applies to all offshore energy installations operating within the Exclusive Economic Zone of Veldrath, including fixed platforms, floating production units, subsea infrastructure, and floating offshore wind installations, with a rated power output exceeding 5 MW.

Article 2. Safety Case Submission
Operators shall submit a Safety Case to the Veldrath Offshore Safety Authority (VOSA) at least 180 days before commencing production operations. The Safety Case shall describe all major hazard scenarios and the control measures in place.

Article 3. Competency Assurance
Operators shall maintain a competency assurance framework for all personnel engaged in safety-critical activities. The framework shall include regular assessment of individual competency against defined role requirements and shall be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 36 months.

Article 4. Emergency Response Plan
Operators shall prepare and maintain an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) covering well control, fire, explosion, hydrocarbon release, and structural failure scenarios. The ERP shall be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 24 months.

Article 5. Well Notification
Prior to the commencement of any well operation, operators shall notify VOSA in writing at least 21 days in advance, providing the well programme, the identity of the well operator, and a summary of the proposed well integrity management measures.

Article 6. Incident Reporting
Operators shall report to VOSA any dangerous occurrence or occupational injury resulting in absence from work exceeding three consecutive days. Reports shall be submitted within 72 hours of the operator becoming aware of the incident.

Article 7. Contractor Safety Obligations
Where operations are carried out wholly or partly by contractors, operators shall ensure that contractors operating safety-critical equipment maintain a competency assurance framework equivalent to that required under Article 3.

Article 8. Records Retention
Operators shall retain all records required under this Directive for a minimum period of five years from the date of creation.

---
Please produce the full obligation delta table in the standard format.

ground_truth.output:
**Orientation**

This delta compares OEISD Edition 3 (Articles 1–7, prior text) against OEISD Edition 4 (Articles 1–8, new text). No regulator-issued change summary was provided; classification relies solely on the two texts.

---

**Delta Table**

| clause-ref | change-type | prior-text summary | new-text summary | action-trigger | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 1 | scope expansion | Applies to fixed platforms, floating production units, and subsea infrastructure >5 MW | Adds "floating offshore wind installations" to the listed installation types | Yes | Net-new test: a compliant operator of a floating offshore wind installation would not previously have been within scope; "floating offshore wind installations" is a new noun in the obligation's object. Checklist trap: the sentence is otherwise identical, but the addition of a new entity class is an expansion, not a restatement. |
| Art. 2 | no substantive change | Safety Case submitted ≥180 days before production; describes major hazard scenarios and controls | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 3 | net-new obligation | Framework includes regular assessment against role requirements | Adds requirement that the framework be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 36 months | Yes | Prior text required maintaining and assessing via the framework but did not require a periodic review of the framework itself. A compliant firm would not already have been required to schedule framework reviews at a fixed interval. The 36-month maximum is a new deadline attached to a new action (framework review). |
| Art. 4 | scope expansion | ERP covers well control, fire, explosion, and hydrocarbon release | ERP now also covers structural failure scenarios | Yes | "Structural failure" is a new noun added to the ERP scope. A compliant operator's ERP would not have been required to address structural failure scenarios. Review interval unchanged. |
| Art. 5 | net-new obligation | Notify VOSA ≥21 days before well operation; provide well programme and well operator identity | Adds requirement to provide a summary of proposed well integrity management measures | Yes-doc | Prior text required notification content: programme and operator identity. New text adds a third required document (well integrity management measures summary). The underlying notification trigger is unchanged; the additional item is a documentation/submission requirement. |
| Art. 6 | no substantive change | Report dangerous occurrence or injury >3 days absence within 72 hours | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 7 (was: n/a — new article) | net-new obligation | No equivalent in Edition 3 | Operators must ensure contractors operating safety-critical equipment maintain a competency assurance framework equivalent to Art. 3 | Yes | Net-new test: Edition 3 imposed the competency assurance obligation only on the operator's own personnel. A compliant operator was not required to verify or mandate equivalent frameworks for contractors. This creates a new due-diligence and oversight obligation directed at a new entity class (contractors). |
| Art. 8 (was: Art. 7) | no substantive change | Retain all records ≥5 years from date of creation | Identical; renumbered from Art. 7 due to insertion of new Art. 7 | No | Subject matter and obligation unchanged; renumbering is a formatting consequence of the inserted article. |

---

**Summary**

| Change-type | Count |
|---|---|
| net-new obligation | 3 |
| scope expansion | 2 |
| clarification / restatement | 0 |
| obligation withdrawn / relaxed | 0 |
| no substantive change | 3 |
| ambiguous — human review | 0 |

**Review-flagged clauses:** None.

**Notes for downstream:** Art. 5 (Yes-doc) and Art. 7-new (Yes) are highest priority. Art. 8's renumbering from Art. 7 should be reflected in internal document cross-references but requires no compliance action.

metadata.name: OEISD Energy Safety Directive — Edition 3 to Edition 4

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly identify the renumbered Art. 8 (was Art. 7) as no substantive change rather than a phantom deletion plus net-new? Does it correctly classify Art. 5 as Yes-doc (documentation expansion) rather than Yes (operational)? Does it distinguish Art. 3's new periodic review interval as genuinely net-new?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Are all eight new-text clauses covered? Are the notes grounded in specific clause elements (new noun 'floating offshore wind installations', '36-month interval', 'structural failure', 'well integrity management measures summary', 'contractors') rather than generic phrases?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response handle the absence of a regulator summary gracefully and still reach correct conclusions from the texts alone?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly treat Art. 7 (new contractor obligation) as net-new with action-trigger Yes, recognising that Edition 3 only addressed operator personnel?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the table ordered by new-text clause reference? Is the summary count accurate?

metadata.judge_notes: The primary trap is Art. 5: the addition of a third required submission item looks like a full net-new obligation but the notification trigger itself is unchanged — only the content of the notification is expanded, making it documentation-only (Yes-doc). A response that marks Art. 5 as Yes (substantive) misclassifies C7. Secondary: Art. 8 renumbered from Art. 7 must appear as a single no-substantive-change row, not as Art. 7 deleted plus Art. 8 new. Any response splitting it into two rows is wrong on C1/C14. Accept minor phrasing variation in notes so long as the specific clause element (e.g. 'floating offshore wind installations', '36-month', 'structural failure', 'contractors', 'well integrity management measures') is named.

input:
Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Veldrath Consumer Credit Disclosure Rules (VCCDR) below. A regulator-issued change summary is included.

---
REGULATOR SUMMARY (Veldrath Financial Services Commission, Circular FSC-2026-14)
---
"The amendments to the VCCDR published in this circular clarify existing disclosure obligations and align the Rules with established supervisory guidance. In particular, the addition of Article 4(c) clarifies what information must be presented prominently. No new substantive obligations are introduced."

---
PRIOR TEXT — VCCDR, Articles 1–5
---

Article 1. Application
These Rules apply to all persons providing consumer credit in Veldrath, including banks, credit unions, and licensed non-bank lenders.

Article 2. Pre-Contractual Disclosure
Before entering into a consumer credit agreement, a lender shall provide the borrower with a standardised pre-contractual information statement containing the total cost of credit, the annual percentage rate, and the repayment schedule.

Article 3. Advertising Standards
Any advertisement for a consumer credit product shall state the annual percentage rate prominently and shall not use misleading comparisons.

Article 4. Contract Terms
(a) Credit agreements shall be set out in plain language accessible to the target consumer.
(b) Any fees or charges not included in the annual percentage rate shall be separately itemised in the agreement.

Article 5. Complaints Handling
Lenders shall maintain a complaints handling procedure and shall resolve complaints within 45 business days of receipt.

---
NEW TEXT — VCCDR (amended), Articles 1–5
---

Article 1. Application
These Rules apply to all persons providing consumer credit in Veldrath, including banks, credit unions, licensed non-bank lenders, and buy-now-pay-later service providers.

Article 2. Pre-Contractual Disclosure
Before entering into a consumer credit agreement, a lender shall provide the borrower with a standardised pre-contractual information statement containing the total cost of credit, the annual percentage rate, and the repayment schedule.

Article 3. Advertising Standards
Any advertisement for a consumer credit product shall state the annual percentage rate prominently and shall not use misleading comparisons.

Article 4. Contract Terms
(a) Credit agreements shall be set out in plain language accessible to the target consumer.
(b) Any fees or charges not included in the annual percentage rate shall be separately itemised in the agreement.
(c) The annual percentage rate and total cost of credit shall be displayed in a font size no smaller than the largest font size used elsewhere in the agreement.

Article 5. Complaints Handling
Lenders shall maintain a complaints handling procedure and shall resolve complaints within 30 business days of receipt.

---
Please produce the full obligation delta table.

ground_truth.output:
**Orientation**

This delta compares VCCDR prior text (Articles 1–5) against the amended VCCDR (Articles 1–5, same numbering). The Veldrath Financial Services Commission Circular FSC-2026-14 was provided and characterises all amendments as clarifications with no new substantive obligations. That characterisation is taken as evidence but not as controlling; the clause texts are examined independently.

---

**Delta Table**

| clause-ref | change-type | prior-text summary | new-text summary | action-trigger | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 1 | scope expansion | Applies to banks, credit unions, and licensed non-bank lenders | Adds "buy-now-pay-later service providers" to the list of obligated persons | Yes | Regulator summary says no new substantive obligations, but the texts decide: "buy-now-pay-later service providers" is a new entity class not previously enumerated. A BNPL provider operating in Veldrath would not have been within scope under the prior text. This is a scope expansion, not a clarification, notwithstanding the circular. |
| Art. 2 | no substantive change | Pre-contractual statement: total cost of credit, APR, repayment schedule | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 3 | no substantive change | Advertisements must state APR prominently; no misleading comparisons | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 4(a) | no substantive change | Agreements in plain language | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 4(b) | no substantive change | Non-APR fees separately itemised | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 4(c) — new | ambiguous — human review | No equivalent in prior text | APR and total cost of credit must appear in a font size no smaller than the largest font size used elsewhere in the agreement | Review | The circular calls this a clarification of "prominent" display. Prior Art. 3 required APR to appear prominently in advertising; prior Art. 4 had no font-size requirement for agreements. Whether Art. 4(c) is a clarification (prominent already implied this standard for agreements) or a net-new obligation (no font-size requirement existed for agreements) depends on whether "prominently" in Art. 3 was ever read to govern agreement text. The texts do not resolve this. Question: Does "prominently" as used in prior Art. 3 extend to agreement formatting, such that a font-size rule for agreements was already implied? If yes → clarification (No trigger); if no → net-new obligation (Yes trigger). |
| Art. 5 | obligation withdrawn / relaxed | Complaints resolved within 45 business days | Complaints resolved within 30 business days | No | The deadline is shortened from 45 to 30 business days. This tightens the obligation, making it a scope expansion or net-new, not a relaxation. Retention: no withdrawal artefacts; this is a tightening. Correction to initial read: a threshold change from 45 to 30 days shortens the permitted resolution window — this is a net-new/scope-expansion (tighter deadline), not a relaxation. Reclassifying: | 

*[Self-correction on Art. 5: the direction of change is a shorter deadline, which is a tightening, not a relaxation. Correct label below.]*

| Art. 5 | scope expansion | Complaints resolved within 45 business days | Complaints resolved within 30 business days | Yes | The permitted resolution window is shortened by 15 business days. A compliant firm operating at the prior 45-day limit would now be in breach. This is a tightened threshold — an expansion of the obligation's burden — not a relaxation. The regulator's circular does not address Art. 5. |

---

**Summary**

| Change-type | Count |
|---|---|
| net-new obligation | 0 |
| scope expansion | 2 (Art. 1, Art. 5) |
| clarification / restatement | 0 |
| obligation withdrawn / relaxed | 0 |
| no substantive change | 4 |
| ambiguous — human review | 1 (Art. 4(c)) |

**Review-flagged clauses:**
- **Art. 4(c):** Does the "prominently" standard in prior Art. 3 extend to agreement text formatting, making the font-size rule a clarification? If yes → No trigger; if no → net-new with Yes trigger.

metadata.name: VCCDR Consumer Credit Rules — Regulator Summary Override and Threshold Tightening

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response override the FSC circular's 'clarification' characterisation for Art. 1 (BNPL providers) and correctly label it scope expansion? Does it correctly identify Art. 5's shortened deadline as a tightening (scope expansion / Yes trigger) rather than a relaxation? Does it reach the right ambiguous label for Art. 4(c) with a specific answerable question?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Are notes grounded in specific clause elements: 'buy-now-pay-later service providers' for Art. 1, '45 to 30 business days' direction for Art. 5, the relationship between prior Art. 3's 'prominently' and new Art. 4(c)'s font-size rule? Generic notes ('this adds requirements') score near zero.
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response handle the regulator summary as evidence-not-controlling for Art. 1 while also recognising the summary's silence on Art. 5 and independently classifying that change?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly distinguish that a shorter deadline is a tightening (not relaxation), resisting the 'threshold change → relaxed' checklist error?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the summary count accurate (2 scope expansions, 4 no-change, 1 review)? Is Art. 4(c) the sole Review row?

metadata.judge_notes: Two traps: (1) The FSC circular says 'no new substantive obligations' but Art. 1 adds BNPL providers — texts decide, correct label is scope expansion (C6 trap). (2) Art. 5 changes deadline from 45 to 30 days — the direction is tightening, not relaxation; a checklist keyed 'threshold change → withdrawn/relaxed' produces the wrong label (C5 trap). The correct label for Art. 5 is scope expansion with Yes trigger. Art. 4(c) is genuinely ambiguous because the prior 'prominently' standard (Art. 3) is limited to advertising and the texts do not resolve whether it governed agreement formatting. Accept the ambiguous label with a question distinguishing clarification from net-new. A response that labels Art. 5 as 'obligation withdrawn/relaxed' or that accepts the circular's framing for Art. 1 fails both traps. The self-correction narrative in the reference output is acceptable; a clean table without the correction narrative also scores full marks if the final label is correct.

input:
Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Medtravar Pharmaceutical Serialisation and Track-and-Trace Requirements (PSTR) below. A regulator explanatory note is included.

---
REGULATOR EXPLANATORY NOTE (Medtravar Medicines Regulatory Agency, MRA-EN-2025-09)
---
"Articles 3 and 4 have been restructured for clarity. The obligations they contain are unchanged; the restructuring reflects supervisory practice as already communicated in MRA Supervisory Letter SL-2023-04, which required manufacturers to notify the MRA of any serialisation system failure within 48 hours."

---
PRIOR TEXT — PSTR, Articles 1–6
---

Article 1. Definitions
"Serialisation" means the assignment of a unique identifier to each saleable unit of a medicinal product.

Article 2. Scope
These Requirements apply to all manufacturers and marketing authorisation holders placing medicinal products on the Medtravar market.

Article 3. Serialisation Obligation
Manufacturers shall assign a unique identifier to each saleable unit before the product is released for distribution.

Article 4. System Integrity
Manufacturers shall take appropriate measures to ensure the integrity of their serialisation systems.

Article 5. Wholesale Distributor Verification
Wholesale distributors shall verify the unique identifier of each medicinal product at the point of receipt from the manufacturer and at the point of supply to a pharmacy or hospital.

Article 6. Records
All parties subject to these Requirements shall maintain records of serialisation transactions for a minimum of three years.

---
NEW TEXT — PSTR (revised), Articles 1–7
---

Article 1. Definitions
"Serialisation" means the assignment of a unique identifier to each saleable unit of a medicinal product.

Article 2. Scope
These Requirements apply to all manufacturers and marketing authorisation holders placing medicinal products on the Medtravar market.

Article 3. Serialisation Obligation
Manufacturers shall assign a unique identifier to each saleable unit before the product is released for distribution.

Article 4. System Integrity
Manufacturers shall take appropriate measures to ensure the integrity of their serialisation systems, including: conducting quarterly system validation tests; maintaining documented procedures for system failure response; and notifying the Medtravar Medicines Regulatory Agency within 48 hours of any system failure that affects the assignment or verification of unique identifiers.

Article 5. Wholesale Distributor Verification
Wholesale distributors shall verify the unique identifier of each medicinal product at the point of receipt from the manufacturer and at the point of supply to a pharmacy or hospital.

Article 6. Marketing Authorisation Holder Audit Rights
Marketing authorisation holders shall conduct or commission an annual audit of the serialisation systems of any contract manufacturer producing medicinal products on their behalf.

Article 7. Records
All parties subject to these Requirements shall maintain records of serialisation transactions for a minimum of three years.

---
Please produce the full obligation delta table.

ground_truth.output:
**Orientation**

This delta compares PSTR prior text (Articles 1–6) against the revised PSTR (Articles 1–7). MRA Explanatory Note MRA-EN-2025-09 was provided; it asserts that Articles 3 and 4 are unchanged in substance and references MRA Supervisory Letter SL-2023-04 (which required 48-hour failure notification). That characterisation is taken as evidence. The clause texts are examined to verify whether the prior cross-reference resolves the classification.

---

**Delta Table**

| clause-ref | change-type | prior-text summary | new-text summary | action-trigger | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 1 | no substantive change | Defines "Serialisation" | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 2 | no substantive change | Applies to manufacturers and marketing authorisation holders | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 3 | no substantive change | Unique identifier assigned before distribution release | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 4 (enumerations) | clarification / restatement | Manufacturers take "appropriate measures" to ensure system integrity | Now enumerates three specific measures: quarterly validation tests, documented failure-response procedures, and 48-hour MRA notification of system failures | Yes-doc | Net-new test applied to each enumerated item. (i) Quarterly validation tests: "appropriate measures" under a general standard would reasonably encompass system validation; this is an enumeration of what the general standard means, not a new verb. (ii) Documented failure-response procedures: prior text's "appropriate measures" in a system-integrity context would be understood to include documented procedures for failure response — this codifies existing supervisory expectation. (iii) 48-hour MRA notification: the MRA Explanatory Note states this was already required by SL-2023-04, a cross-referenced supervisory instrument. The texts support this: SL-2023-04 is cited as the source. A compliant firm was already required to notify within 48 hours. All three enumerations are clarifications of the prior general standard, borne out by the explanatory note and the cross-reference. Action-trigger is Yes-doc: firms must now document their validation schedule and failure-response procedures explicitly to demonstrate compliance with the enumerated standard. |
| Art. 5 | no substantive change | Wholesale distributors verify unique identifiers at receipt and supply | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 6 (was: n/a — new article) | net-new obligation | No equivalent in prior text | Marketing authorisation holders must conduct or commission an annual audit of contract manufacturers' serialisation systems | Yes | Net-new test: the prior text imposed no audit obligation on marketing authorisation holders vis-à-vis contract manufacturers. A compliant MAH was not required to audit or commission audits of contract manufacturer serialisation systems. "Annual audit" is a new verb of action directed at a relationship (MAH → contract manufacturer) not previously regulated. The explanatory note does not address this article. |
| Art. 7 (was: Art. 6) | no substantive change | All parties maintain serialisation records ≥3 years | Identical; renumbered from Art. 6 due to insertion of new Art. 6 | No | Subject matter and retention period unchanged. Renumbering is a formatting consequence of the inserted article. |

---

**Summary**

| Change-type | Count |
|---|---|
| net-new obligation | 1 (Art. 6) |
| scope expansion | 0 |
| clarification / restatement | 1 (Art. 4) |
| obligation withdrawn / relaxed | 0 |
| no substantive change | 4 |
| ambiguous — human review | 0 |

**Review-flagged clauses:** None.

**Notes for downstream:** Art. 4's Yes-doc trigger means firms must produce written validation schedules and failure-response procedures even if the underlying practices already exist. Art. 6 (new) is the sole substantive new obligation and should be routed to the MAH compliance owner.

metadata.name: PSTR Pharmaceutical Serialisation — Cross-Reference Clarification vs. Net-New Audit

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly classify Art. 4's enumeration (including 48-hour notification) as clarification/restatement rather than net-new, citing SL-2023-04 cross-reference as the basis? Does it correctly identify Art. 6 (new MAH audit obligation) as genuinely net-new? Does it handle the renumbering of Art. 7 correctly?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Notes must name the specific elements: 'quarterly validation tests', 'SL-2023-04' for the 48-hour item, 'annual audit of contract manufacturer serialisation systems' for Art. 6. Generic notes ('adds requirements') score near zero.
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response use the regulator's explanatory note appropriately — accepting it for the cross-reference item (48-hour notification) while independently evaluating Art. 6 which the note does not address?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly identify Yes-doc (not Yes) for Art. 4, recognising that the underlying practices were already required but documentation evidence must now be explicit?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the summary correct: 1 net-new, 1 clarification, 4 no-change, 0 review? Is Art. 7's renumbering shown as '(was: Art. 6)'?

metadata.judge_notes: The primary trap is Art. 4: a keyword scan sees 'quarterly validation tests' and 'notify within 48 hours' as new verbs and flags net-new, but the net-new test shows (a) general standard already covered validation, (b) SL-2023-04 already required 48-hour notification. Correct label is clarification with Yes-doc (documentation evidence must now be explicit). The cross-reference to SL-2023-04 is named in the explanatory note and must be cited in the notes column — a response that says 'general standard already covered this' without mentioning SL-2023-04 for the notification item is grounded but incomplete; accept if SL-2023-04 is at least mentioned for item (iii). Art. 6 is genuinely net-new and the response must identify the new verb ('conduct or commission an annual audit') and the new obligated relationship (MAH → contract manufacturer). Art. 7 renumbered from Art. 6 must be a single no-substantive-change row.

Please extract the obligation delta for the following regulatory texts. Note that only the new text has been provided.

---
NEW TEXT — Belcorian Data Residency Ordinance (BDRO), Articles 1–6 (2026 Revision)
---

Article 1. Purpose
This Ordinance establishes data residency requirements for personal data of Belcorian residents processed by digital service providers.

Article 2. Scope
This Ordinance applies to digital service providers with more than 10,000 active Belcorian user accounts.

Article 3. Data Residency Obligation
Personal data of Belcorian residents shall be stored on servers physically located within the territory of Belcor.

Article 4. Transfer Restriction
Personal data shall not be transferred outside Belcor unless the recipient jurisdiction has been designated as adequate by the Belcorian Data Authority.

Article 5. Audit Right
The Belcorian Data Authority may conduct or commission audits of digital service providers to verify compliance with Articles 3 and 4.

Article 6. Penalties
Breaches of this Ordinance may result in fines of up to 2% of global annual turnover.

---
No prior text has been provided. Please produce the obligation delta.

ground_truth.output:
**Stop — prior text is missing.**

I cannot produce an obligation delta table. A delta requires both a prior text and a new text; only the new text (Belcorian Data Residency Ordinance 2026 Revision, Articles 1–6) has been provided.

I will not reconstruct or infer a prior version of the BDRO from memory or from similar data-residency frameworks. Even where an earlier edition of a regulation is publicly known, prior and new texts that appear nearly identical can conceal obligation shifts, and manufacturing the prior text would risk misclassifying genuine changes as clarifications or vice versa.

**To proceed, please provide:**
- The prior version of the Belcorian Data Residency Ordinance (the edition this 2026 Revision supersedes), pasted in full or attached.

Once both texts are available, I will produce the orientation paragraph, delta table, and summary in the standard format.

metadata.name: BDRO Data Residency — Missing Prior Text Stop Condition

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly identify that the prior text is absent and that reconstruction from memory is not permissible, even for a regulation that might be familiar? Does it resist the temptation to 'helpfully' generate a plausible prior text?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Is the stop response clean and actionable — naming exactly what is needed (the prior edition of the BDRO) without producing any partial delta or speculative content?
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response explain WHY reconstruction is dangerous (obligation shifts hidden in near-identical text), not just that it cannot be done? This shows genuine understanding rather than a hard-coded stop rule.
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response avoid hallucinating a prior BDRO version or extrapolating from similar data-residency frameworks in other jurisdictions?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the response concise and directive — telling the user specifically what to provide to unblock the process?

metadata.judge_notes: This is a stop-condition scenario (C12). The correct output is to ask for the missing prior text and explain why reconstruction is not permissible. A response that produces any partial delta table — even a 'tentative' one — is wrong regardless of how plausible the content seems. A response that stops but gives no reason beyond 'I need both texts' is acceptable but partial; full marks require at least a one-sentence explanation of why reconstruction is unreliable. Do NOT penalise for brevity; a short, clean stop response is better than a long one that hedges.

input:
Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Narrath Waste Classification and Disposal Regulations (WCDR) below. A regulator change summary is included.

---
REGULATOR CHANGE SUMMARY (Narrath Environmental Standards Office, ESO Notice 2026-03)
---
"The amendment to WCDR Regulation 5 removes the small-quantity generator exemption. This amendment clarifies the scope of the Regulation by aligning it with the treatment of small-quantity generators under the Narrath Hazardous Materials Framework (NHMF), which already subjected them to equivalent obligations."

---
PRIOR TEXT — WCDR, Regulations 1–6
---

Regulation 1. Interpretation
"Hazardous waste" means any waste that exhibits ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity, or toxicity as defined in Schedule A.

Regulation 2. Waste Manifest
All persons generating hazardous waste shall complete a waste manifest before transferring hazardous waste to a licensed carrier.

Regulation 3. Licensed Carrier Requirement
Hazardous waste shall only be transported by carriers holding a valid licence issued by the Narrath Environmental Standards Office.

Regulation 4. Treatment and Disposal
Hazardous waste shall be treated and disposed of at a facility authorised by the Narrath Environmental Standards Office.

Regulation 5. Scope Exemption
Regulations 2, 3, and 4 shall not apply to small-quantity generators, being persons generating less than 25 kilograms of hazardous waste per calendar month.

Regulation 6. Records
All persons subject to these Regulations shall maintain records of waste manifests and disposal certificates for a minimum of four years.

---
NEW TEXT — WCDR (amended), Regulations 1–5
---

Regulation 1. Interpretation
"Hazardous waste" means any waste that exhibits ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity, or toxicity as defined in Schedule A.

Regulation 2. Waste Manifest
All persons generating hazardous waste shall complete a waste manifest before transferring hazardous waste to a licensed carrier.

Regulation 3. Licensed Carrier Requirement
Hazardous waste shall only be transported by carriers holding a valid licence issued by the Narrath Environmental Standards Office.

Regulation 4. Treatment and Disposal
Hazardous waste shall be treated and disposed of at a facility authorised by the Narrath Environmental Standards Office.

Regulation 5. Records
All persons subject to these Regulations shall maintain records of waste manifests and disposal certificates for a minimum of four years.

---
Please produce the full obligation delta table.

ground_truth.output:
**Orientation**

This delta compares WCDR prior text (Regulations 1–6) against the amended WCDR (Regulations 1–5). ESO Notice 2026-03 was provided; it characterises the removal of Regulation 5's small-quantity generator exemption as a "clarification" aligning with the NHMF. That characterisation is taken as evidence. The clause texts are examined to determine whether removing an express exemption is a clarification or a scope expansion.

---

**Delta Table**

| clause-ref | change-type | prior-text summary | new-text summary | action-trigger | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reg. 1 | no substantive change | Defines "hazardous waste" | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Reg. 2 | no substantive change | Waste manifest required before transfer to licensed carrier | Identical | No | Wording unchanged; prior exemption under old Reg. 5 is addressed separately. |
| Reg. 3 | no substantive change | Transport only by ESO-licensed carrier | Identical | No | Wording unchanged; prior exemption addressed separately. |
| Reg. 4 | no substantive change | Treatment and disposal at ESO-authorised facility | Identical | No | Wording unchanged; prior exemption addressed separately. |
| Reg. 5 (was: Reg. 6) | no substantive change | Records of manifests and disposal certificates retained ≥4 years | Identical; renumbered from Reg. 6 following deletion of prior Reg. 5 | No | Subject matter unchanged. Renumbering is a consequence of the deletion. |
| Prior Reg. 5 — scope expansion (withdrawal of exemption) | scope expansion | Regulations 2, 3, and 4 did not apply to small-quantity generators (<25 kg/month) | Exemption deleted; small-quantity generators are now subject to Regulations 2, 3, and 4 | Yes | The ESO Notice characterises this as a "clarification" because NHMF already subjected small-quantity generators to equivalent obligations. The texts decide: removing an express exemption is an expansion signal regardless of parallel obligations in another instrument. The NHMF cross-reference does not appear in WCDR's prior or new text; a small-quantity generator was not required to comply with WCDR Regulations 2–4 under the prior text, whatever the NHMF said. The removal of the explicit <25 kg/month exemption brings a new class of generators within scope. Correct label: scope expansion. Net-new test: a small-quantity generator complying only with WCDR (not separately with NHMF) would not previously have been required to complete a waste manifest, use a licensed carrier, or use an authorised disposal facility under this instrument. The ESO Notice cannot convert an exemption removal into a clarification. |

---

| Change-type | Count |
|---|---|

| scope expansion | 1 (prior Reg. 5 — exemption removal) |
| clarification / restatement | 0 |
| obligation withdrawn / relaxed | 0 |
| no substantive change | 5 |
| ambiguous — human review | 0 |

**Review-flagged clauses:** None.

**Notes for downstream:** The scope expansion is high-priority for any client with small-quantity generator operations (<25 kg/month). Those entities must now implement waste manifests, licensed-carrier arrangements, and authorised disposal facility relationships. The ESO Notice's reference to NHMF alignment may be relevant context for transition but does not alter the WCDR compliance obligation.

metadata.name: WCDR Waste Classification — Exemption Removal Mislabelled as Clarification

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response override the ESO Notice's 'clarification' characterisation and correctly label the exemption removal as scope expansion? Does it articulate that the NHMF cross-reference appears in the regulator notice but not in the WCDR texts, and therefore cannot render the WCDR exemption removal a clarification within this instrument? Does it handle the renumbering of Reg. 6 → Reg. 5 correctly?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Notes must name: 'small-quantity generators (<25 kg/month)', 'exemption deleted', and the net-new test result (generators were not required under WCDR Regulations 2–4 under prior text). Generic notes score near zero.
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response correctly note that the NHMF cross-reference appears only in the ESO Notice, not in the WCDR texts themselves, distinguishing it from a cross-reference within the instrument?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly identify that Regulations 2, 3, and 4 are textually unchanged but that their operative scope has expanded due to the exemption removal — and handle this by attributing the expansion to the deleted Reg. 5 row?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the summary count correct (1 scope expansion, 5 no-change)? Is the renumbering shown for Reg. 5 (was Reg. 6)?

metadata.judge_notes: The decisive trap: ESO Notice says 'clarification' but the prior Reg. 5 was an explicit exemption. The NHMF cross-reference in the notice is not found in the WCDR texts themselves; a response that treats the NHMF reference as a within-instrument cross-reference (like SL-2023-04 in S-003) and classifies the change as clarification is wrong. The correct label is scope expansion because: (1) removing an explicit exemption is an expansion signal per the taxonomy, and (2) the NHMF cross-reference is external to the WCDR instrument and appears only in the regulator's notice. The response must also correctly handle the deletion of prior Reg. 5 (the exemption) and the renumbering of prior Reg. 6 to new Reg. 5. A response that creates a phantom deletion row for old Reg. 5 and a phantom addition for new Reg. 5 (thinking they are different subjects) fails C1.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Calveth Investment Adviser Conduct Standards (CIACS) below. No regulator summary has been provided.

---
PRIOR TEXT — CIACS, Standards 1–7
---

Standard 1. Fiduciary Duty
Investment advisers shall act in the best interests of their clients and shall disclose any material conflicts of interest.

Standard 2. Suitability Assessment
Before making a recommendation, investment advisers shall assess whether the recommended product or strategy is suitable for the client, having regard to the client's financial situation, investment objectives, and risk tolerance.

Standard 3. Client Agreement
Investment advisers shall enter into a written client agreement before providing advice. The agreement shall set out the basis of the adviser's remuneration.

Standard 4. Record of Advice
Investment advisers shall maintain a record of each recommendation made and the basis for it.

Standard 5. Continuing Education
Investment advisers shall complete a minimum of 20 hours of continuing professional education per calendar year, at least 10 of which must relate to the Calveth regulatory framework.

Standard 6. Complaint Escalation
Where a complaint is not resolved within 30 days, the investment adviser shall notify the Calveth Financial Conduct Authority (CFCA) and provide a summary of the complaint and steps taken.

Standard 7. Record Retention
All records required under these Standards shall be retained for a minimum of seven years.

---
NEW TEXT — CIACS (revised), Standards 1–7
---

Standard 1. Fiduciary Duty
Investment advisers shall act in the best interests of their clients and shall disclose any material conflicts of interest.

Standard 2. Suitability Assessment
Before making a recommendation, investment advisers shall assess whether the recommended product or strategy is suitable for the client, having regard to the client's financial situation, investment objectives, risk tolerance, and sustainability preferences.

Standard 3. Client Agreement
Investment advisers shall enter into a written client agreement before providing advice. The agreement shall set out the basis of the adviser's remuneration.

Standard 4. Record of Advice
Investment advisers shall maintain a record of each recommendation made, the basis for it, and a note of any sustainability preferences expressed by the client and how those preferences were taken into account.

Standard 5. Continuing Education
Investment advisers shall complete a minimum of 20 hours of continuing professional education per calendar year, at least 10 of which must relate to the Calveth regulatory framework.

Standard 6. Complaint Escalation
Where a complaint is not resolved within 60 days, the investment adviser shall notify the Calveth Financial Conduct Authority (CFCA) and provide a summary of the complaint and steps taken.

Standard 7. Record Retention
All records required under these Standards shall be retained for a minimum of seven years.

---

ground_truth.output:
**Orientation**

This delta compares CIACS prior text (Standards 1–7) against the revised CIACS (Standards 1–7, same numbering). No regulator-issued change summary was provided; classification relies solely on the two texts.

---

**Delta Table**

| clause-ref | change-type | prior-text summary | new-text summary | action-trigger | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Std. 1 | no substantive change | Act in best interests; disclose material conflicts | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Std. 2 | scope expansion | Suitability assessed against financial situation, investment objectives, and risk tolerance | Adds "sustainability preferences" as a fourth suitability criterion | Yes | "Sustainability preferences" is a new noun added to the assessment object. A compliant adviser under prior Std. 2 was not required to assess or document a client's sustainability preferences as a suitability criterion. The new criterion creates an operational obligation: advisers must elicit, document, and consider sustainability preferences before making any recommendation. |
| Std. 3 | no substantive change | Written client agreement; remuneration basis stated | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Std. 4 | net-new obligation | Record of recommendation and basis | Adds obligation to record client's sustainability preferences as expressed and how they were taken into account in each recommendation | Yes-doc | Net-new test: prior Std. 4 required a record of the recommendation and basis only. New Std. 4 adds two new recording items: (i) sustainability preferences expressed by the client, and (ii) how those preferences were taken into account. These are new documentation obligations that did not exist under prior text. The underlying advisory action is expanded by Std. 2; this standard adds the evidence trail. Yes-doc: the change is to the record content, not the creation of a new operational process (which is captured at Std. 2). |
| Std. 5 | no substantive change | 20 hours CPE per year; ≥10 hours Calveth framework | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Std. 6 | obligation withdrawn / relaxed | Notify CFCA if complaint unresolved after 30 days | Notify CFCA if complaint unresolved after 60 days | No | The escalation trigger moves from 30 days to 60 days. This relaxes the obligation by giving advisers 30 additional days before mandatory CFCA notification is required. A compliant firm operating at the prior 30-day trigger would no longer need to notify at that point. Retention: no compliance artefacts to retire — the change affects a trigger threshold, not a record-keeping or filing requirement. Prior records of CFCA notifications made under the 30-day rule do not require ongoing maintenance as a result of this change. |
| Std. 7 | no substantive change | Records retained ≥7 years | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |

---

**Summary**

| Change-type | Count |
|---|---|
| net-new obligation | 1 (Std. 4) |
| scope expansion | 1 (Std. 2) |
| clarification / restatement | 0 |
| obligation withdrawn / relaxed | 1 (Std. 6) |
| no substantive change | 4 |
| ambiguous — human review | 0 |

**Review-flagged clauses:** None.

**Notes for downstream:** Std. 2 (scope expansion, Yes) is the primary operational change — advisers must build sustainability-preference elicitation into the suitability process. Std. 4 (Yes-doc) is the evidence-trail correlate. Std. 6's relaxation reduces escalation burden but compliance teams should update their complaint-handling procedures to reflect the new 60-day trigger.

metadata.name: CIACS Investment Adviser Standards — Threshold Relaxation and Paired Expansion

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly identify Std. 6's 30→60 day change as a relaxation (not a tightening)? Does it correctly separate Std. 2 (scope expansion, Yes) from Std. 4 (net-new documentation obligation, Yes-doc), recognising they are paired but distinct? Does it address retention for the Std. 6 withdrawal correctly?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Notes must name specific elements: 'sustainability preferences' as new noun in Std. 2; '30 additional days before CFCA notification' for Std. 6; the two new recording items in Std. 4 ('sustainability preferences expressed' and 'how taken into account'). Generic notes score near zero.
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response handle the paired nature of Std. 2 and Std. 4 correctly — not collapsing them into one row, but recognising that Std. 4 is a documentation correlate of the Std. 2 expansion?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly address the retention question for Std. 6 — noting that prior CFCA notification records do not need ongoing maintenance, and that no transition clause is referenced because the change is to a trigger threshold?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the summary count accurate (1 net-new, 1 scope expansion, 1 withdrawn/relaxed, 4 no-change)?

metadata.judge_notes: The primary trap is Std. 6: the deadline moves from 30 to 60 days, which is a relaxation (not a tightening). A checklist keyed 'threshold change → net-new' or 'changed deadline → scope expansion' produces the wrong label. Correct label is obligation withdrawn/relaxed with No trigger. Secondary judgment: Std. 4 is Yes-doc (not Yes) because it adds recording obligations for the sustainability-preference process established in Std. 2, not a new operational process itself. A response that marks Std. 4 as Yes collapses the Yes/Yes-doc distinction. Retention for Std. 6 should note that the change is to a trigger threshold and no ongoing records artefact requires maintenance — there is no transition clause in the text to cite, and the response should say so rather than inventing one.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Ferrath Grid Operator Balancing Obligations (GOBO) below. No regulator summary has been provided.

---
PRIOR TEXT — GOBO, Sections 1–5
---

Section 1. Definitions
"Imbalance" means the difference between a market participant's declared schedule and its actual metered position during a settlement period.

Section 2. Balancing Notification
Market participants shall submit balancing notifications to the Ferrath Grid Operator (FGO) covering each settlement period no later than 60 minutes before the start of that period.

Section 3. Imbalance Settlement
The FGO shall calculate each market participant's imbalance for each settlement period and shall apply the imbalance settlement price published for that period.

Section 4. Metering Data Submission
Market participants shall submit metered data to the FGO within 10 business days of the end of each month.

Section 5. Record Keeping
Market participants shall retain records of all balancing notifications and metered data submissions for a period of six years.

---
NEW TEXT — GOBO (amended), Sections 1–5
---

Section 1. Definitions
"Imbalance" means the difference between a market participant's declared schedule and its actual metered position during a settlement period. "Aggregator" means a person who combines the flexible capacity of multiple end-users and participates in balancing markets on their behalf.

Section 2. Balancing Notification
Market participants, including aggregators acting on behalf of end-users, shall submit balancing notifications to the Ferrath Grid Operator (FGO) covering each settlement period no later than 60 minutes before the start of that period.

Section 3. Imbalance Settlement
The FGO shall calculate each market participant's imbalance for each settlement period and shall apply the imbalance settlement price published for that period.

Section 4. Metering Data Submission
Market participants shall submit metered data to the FGO within 10 business days of the end of each month.

Section 5. Record Keeping
Market participants shall retain records of all balancing notifications and metered data submissions for a period of six years.

---

**Orientation**

This delta compares GOBO prior text (Sections 1–5) against the amended GOBO (Sections 1–5, same numbering). No regulator-issued change summary was provided; classification relies solely on the two texts.

---

**Delta Table**

| clause-ref | change-type | prior-text summary | new-text summary | action-trigger | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sec. 1 | scope expansion | Defines "Imbalance" only | Adds definition of "Aggregator": a person combining flexible capacity of multiple end-users to participate in balancing markets | Yes | The addition of the "Aggregator" definition is not merely a typographical addition: "Aggregator" is used operatively in Section 2, where it is now included as a category of market participant subject to the balancing notification obligation. A definition that expands the operative scope of an existing obligation by bringing a new entity class within it is a scope expansion, not a standalone clarification. Net-new test: an aggregator operating in Ferrath would not previously have been expressly obligated under GOBO; the prior text's "market participants" may not have been read to include aggregators unambiguously. Grounded in: "Aggregator" as new entity class whose inclusion in Sec. 2 is operative. |
| Sec. 2 | scope expansion | Market participants submit balancing notifications ≥60 min before settlement period | Same obligation, now expressly including "aggregators acting on behalf of end-users" | Yes | The new text's express inclusion of aggregators in Section 2 is an expansion of scope to a new entity class. Even if aggregators were arguably "market participants" under prior text, their express inclusion alongside a new definition resolves any ambiguity in the direction of bringing them within scope. A compliant aggregator may not previously have treated itself as subject to the 60-minute notification obligation. Action-trigger Yes: requires aggregators to establish or adapt balancing notification processes. |
| Sec. 3 | no substantive change | FGO calculates imbalance and applies imbalance settlement price | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Sec. 4 | no substantive change | Metered data submitted within 10 business days of month-end | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Sec. 5 | no substantive change | Records retained for six years | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |

---

**Summary**

| Change-type | Count |
|---|---|
| net-new obligation | 0 |
| scope expansion | 2 (Sec. 1, Sec. 2) |
| clarification / restatement | 0 |
| obligation withdrawn / relaxed | 0 |
| no substantive change | 3 |
| ambiguous — human review | 0 |

**Review-flagged clauses:** None.

**Notes for downstream:** Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 together constitute a coordinated scope expansion targeting aggregators. The operative effect is that aggregators must now submit balancing notifications to FGO within the same 60-minute window as other market participants. Steps 3–5 are unaffected.

metadata.name: GOBO Grid Balancing — Definition Addition Triggering Scope Expansion

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response recognise that the 'Aggregator' definition is not a standalone clarification but is coupled with Sec. 2's operative inclusion of aggregators, making both Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 scope expansions? Does it resist classifying Sec. 1 as a mere definition addition (clarification) and trace its operative effect?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Notes must name 'Aggregator' as the new entity class and explain that Sec. 2's express inclusion is operative. Notes on Sec. 2 must reference 'aggregators acting on behalf of end-users' and the 60-minute notification obligation.
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response correctly identify that the prior 'market participants' formulation may have been ambiguous regarding aggregators, and that the new text resolves that ambiguity in the direction of inclusion (expansion)?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly classify Sec. 3–5 as no substantive change and avoid inflating them?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the summary count correct (2 scope expansions, 3 no-change)? Is the table ordered by section number?

metadata.judge_notes: The key judgment is recognising that a definition addition is only a clarification when the term was already operative and the definition merely codifies its understood meaning. Here 'Aggregator' is a new entity class whose definition directly enables Sec. 2 to capture them. A response that labels Sec. 1 as 'clarification' (definition of existing term) misses that 'Aggregator' was not used in prior text at all — it is a new term whose definition creates the operative hook for Sec. 2. Both Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 should be scope expansion; a response that only marks Sec. 2 as scope expansion and Sec. 1 as clarification is partially correct but misses the coordinated nature of the change. Sec. 3–5 are straightforwardly no substantive change and should not be inflated.

Clause 3 is the only clause without a substantive change (the certification mark permission is not extended or restricted). Priority for importers: Clause 2 (conformity assessment before market placement) is the gate obligation; Clauses 4–6 follow from it operationally.

metadata.judge_notes: This scenario tests C5 (expansion signals) and C2 (taxonomy) with a systematic, non-stacked change. The correct judgment is scope expansion at every affected clause (Cl. 1, 2, 4, 5, 6) because 'importers' is a new entity class. A response that labels these as net-new obligation is wrong (the obligations themselves are not new — their extension to a new entity class is the expansion). A response that collapses all five into a single row fails C10 (one row per changed clause). Cl. 3 is the discriminating row: the certification mark is permissive and is not extended to importers in the new text — it simply continues to apply to products that have undergone conformity assessment, now including those assessed by importers. A response that marks Cl. 3 as scope expansion (because importers can now also use the mark) misreads the clause; the mark is tied to the assessment process, not to a named entity class.

---
REGULATOR EXPLANATORY MEMORANDUM (Sentavo Communications Authority, SCA-EM-2026-02)
---
"Article 4 has been amended to require providers to document their lawful interception capability assessments. This requirement reflects the existing obligation under SCA Operational Guidance OG-2024-17 to maintain such assessments and aligns the written Rules with established practice."

PRIOR TEXT — ECIR, Articles 1–5
---

Article 1. Scope
These Rules apply to publicly available electronic communications service providers operating networks in Sentavo.

Article 2. Lawful Interception Capability
Providers shall maintain the technical and organisational capability to intercept electronic communications upon receipt of a valid authority issued by the Sentavo Security Directorate.

Article 3. Interception Handover Interface
Providers shall maintain a handover interface conforming to the technical specifications published by the Sentavo Communications Authority.

Article 4. Capability Assessment
Providers shall assess their lawful interception capability at intervals not exceeding 12 months and shall take corrective action where deficiencies are identified.

Article 5. Confidentiality
Providers shall not disclose to any person other than the Sentavo Security Directorate the existence or content of any interception authority.

---
NEW TEXT — ECIR (amended), Articles 1–6
---

Article 1. Scope
These Rules apply to publicly available electronic communications service providers operating networks in Sentavo.

Article 2. Lawful Interception Capability
Providers shall maintain the technical and organisational capability to intercept electronic communications upon receipt of a valid authority issued by the Sentavo Security Directorate.

Article 3. Interception Handover Interface
Providers shall maintain a handover interface conforming to the technical specifications published by the Sentavo Communications Authority.

Article 4. Capability Assessment
Providers shall assess their lawful interception capability at intervals not exceeding 12 months, shall document each assessment in a written report, and shall take corrective action where deficiencies are identified.

Article 5. New Provider Notification
A provider that commences operation of a new network segment shall notify the Sentavo Communications Authority within 30 days and shall submit a capability assessment for the new segment within 90 days of commencement.

Article 6. Confidentiality
Providers shall not disclose to any person other than the Sentavo Security Directorate the existence or content of any interception authority.

ground_truth.output:
**Orientation**

This delta compares ECIR prior text (Articles 1–5) against the amended ECIR (Articles 1–6). SCA Explanatory Memorandum SCA-EM-2026-02 was provided; it characterises Art. 4's documentation requirement as reflecting existing practice under SCA Operational Guidance OG-2024-17 and does not address Art. 5 (new). The texts are examined independently.

---

**Delta Table**

| clause-ref | change-type | prior-text summary | new-text summary | action-trigger | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Art. 1 | no substantive change | Applies to publicly available ECS providers in Sentavo | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 2 | no substantive change | Maintain LI capability; execute on valid SSD authority | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 3 | no substantive change | Handover interface conforming to SCA technical specs | Identical | No | Wording unchanged. |
| Art. 4 | clarification / restatement | Assess LI capability ≤12 months; take corrective action on deficiencies | Adds "shall document each assessment in a written report" | Yes-doc | The SCA-EM states OG-2024-17 already required providers to maintain such assessments, and the texts are consistent with this: the annual assessment obligation existed in prior Art. 4, and OG-2024-17 (a cross-referenced SCA instrument within the same regulatory framework) already required documentation. Net-new test: a provider complying with prior Art. 4 and OG-2024-17 was already required to document capability assessments. The new text's "written report" requirement codifies that existing practice in the Rules themselves. Correct label: clarification. Action-trigger Yes-doc: providers must now ensure the written report is produced as a ECIR-level artefact (not only under OG-2024-17), which may affect the evidentiary standard required. |
| Art. 5 (new) | net-new obligation | No equivalent in prior text | New providers commencing a network segment must notify SCA within 30 days and submit a capability assessment within 90 days | Yes | Net-new test: prior ECIR contained no notification obligation for new network segments. A compliant provider opening a new segment was not required to notify SCA or submit a segment-specific capability assessment within fixed deadlines. Two new obligations: (i) 30-day notification (new verb of action + new deadline) and (ii) 90-day capability assessment submission for the new segment. The SCA-EM does not address this article. |
| Art. 6 (was: Art. 5) | no substantive change | Confidentiality of interception authority | Identical; renumbered from Art. 5 due to insertion of new Art. 5 | No | Subject matter unchanged. |

---

**Summary**

| Change-type | Count |
|---|---|
| net-new obligation | 1 (Art. 5 new) |
| scope expansion | 0 |
| clarification / restatement | 1 (Art. 4) |
| obligation withdrawn / relaxed | 0 |
| no substantive change | 4 |
| ambiguous — human review | 0 |

**Review-flagged clauses:** None.

**Notes for downstream:** Art. 4 (Yes-doc) requires providers to formalise written capability assessment reports at the ECIR level, even if OG-2024-17 compliance already produces equivalent documents. Art. 5 (new, Yes) is the priority operational change: providers must establish a process for notifying SCA within 30 days of commencing any new network segment and commissioning a segment capability assessment within 90 days.

metadata.name: ECIR Electronic Communications — Cross-Reference Clarification vs. Genuine Notification Net-New

rubric_descriptions.contextual_judgment: Does the response correctly classify Art. 4's 'document each assessment' addition as clarification (citing OG-2024-17) rather than net-new? Does it correctly identify Art. 5 (new) as genuinely net-new — the SCA-EM is silent on it and no cross-reference covers the 30-day/90-day notification obligations? Does it handle Art. 6's renumbering correctly?
rubric_descriptions.output_quality: Notes for Art. 4 must name OG-2024-17 as the cross-reference that already required documentation. Notes for Art. 5 must name both obligations: '30-day notification' and '90-day capability assessment for the new segment'. Generic notes score near zero.
rubric_descriptions.adaptability: Does the response use the SCA-EM appropriately for Art. 4 (accept it, verified by cross-reference) while recognising the SCA-EM says nothing about Art. 5 and classifying it independently?
rubric_descriptions.domain_knowledge: Does the response correctly assign Yes-doc to Art. 4 (not No and not Yes), recognising that the documentation obligation may change the evidentiary standard even if the underlying assessment was already being done?
rubric_descriptions.communication: Is the summary count accurate (1 net-new, 1 clarification, 4 no-change)? Is Art. 6 renaming notation shown?

metadata.judge_notes: The distinguishing judgment: Art. 4's 'document' verb is a clarification because OG-2024-17 already required it (cross-reference confirmed by SCA-EM) — this is the mirror of S-003 (PSTR) where SL-2023-04 covered notification. Art. 5 (new) is genuinely net-new: no cross-reference, no prior general standard, two specific new deadlines (30 and 90 days). A response that labels Art. 4 as net-new (keyword: 'document' = new verb) misses the cross-reference; a response that dismisses Art. 5 as also covered by OG-2024-17 (without textual basis) inflates the cross-reference. The correct split is Art. 4 clarification + Art. 5 net-new. Note: the action-trigger for Art. 4 is Yes-doc not No, because formalisation at the ECIR level may require updated record-keeping procedures even if the underlying assessment exists.
